newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey's Yilmaz says he favours polls next spring.
newsitem.headline: Turkey's Yilmaz says he favours polls next spring.

text.p: Turkish prime minister-designate Mesut Yilmaz said on Friday he favoured early elections in the spring of 1998 to clear up months of political chaos.
"We are in favour of holding general and local elections together next spring," he told a news conference after being asked by President Suleyman Demirel to form a new government.
Yilmaz said he would submit a government list to the president by June 30 to end a political crisis which came to a head on Wednesday with the resignation of Necmettin Erbakan.
Erbakan, Turkey's first Islamist leader, had resigned under military pressure and proposed a coalition led by Ciller to lead the country to early elections.
Yilmaz's Motherland Party has only 129 deputies in the 550-seat parliament and may struggle to find enough allies from the squabbling secularist factions to win a confidence vote.

Two leftist parties have pledged their support for Yilmaz but a secularist alliance would still need backing from a small right-wing group and around a dozen defections from Tansu Ciller's True Path Party.
